scope: Editorial decisions for the paired-biosignal batch’s completed pilots (handoff index status checked 2026-10-12), published together on one topic page of small pilots that stay outside every leaderboard and model ranking. Its own manifest: it amends no earlier review and changes no released file. Orthosis (Zenodo 8345429): one cohort of 8 people, 83 runs and 2,407 events, published as three results — the 64-channel classical baseline, the matched 58-channel classical configuration and frozen EEGPT against that matched configuration — counted once. BINGO (Greek and English inner speech): a cross-person, cross-language spectral-ridge pilot near its prior. Handwriting (EEG-fNIRS competition dataset, EEG only): the mask-aware analysis, published as aggregates by the owner’s decision with its rights gap stated: no ethics-approval or informed-consent statement was found. REFED: the stored-clip computational diagnostic. Status only, with no figure: Orthosis EMG, TinyMyo and EEG–EMG fusion; handwriting fNIRS and fusion; REFED physiological and fusion evaluation; the meditation dataset. The website inputs are the approved aggregate export JSONs only; the handoffs, approvals, QA records and independent audits they cite are pinned by SHA-256 and checked by the export, never copied, because they carry private storage paths. Rights evidence was read by this session from each source’s official record and is kept under evidence/ (git-ignored), pinned here.

approval.basis: The owner’s request in chat on 2026-10-12, relayed by the workflow: prepare the next site version from the handoff index and the new project files. Owner decisions relayed with it: a pilot-studies topic page with a home card, all four pilots outside leaderboards and rankings; publish the Orthosis frozen-EEGPT versus matched 58-channel comparison from its approved export, with the EEGPT checkpoint licence unresolved and no weights distributed; publish BINGO’s aggregates with its rights stated exactly (working default, confirmed at preview), as a single switch; local build only, preview before any deployment. A later owner decision of the same day, relayed by the workflow: publish the handwriting aggregates and state the gap honestly — no ethics-approval or informed-consent statement was found. Each source’s own final approval record approves its aggregate export; this record is the publishing review on top of those, not a replacement for them.
decisionsOfThisReview: Orthosis: the three results are one cohort (8 people, 83 runs, 2,407 events) and are never added to coverage. The 64-channel result stays; the 58-channel configuration and the EEGPT comparison are labelled as configurations of it. The 58-channel rows in the EEGPT export must equal the separately approved classical export exactly.

Orthosis: the response-clean subset is published as counts only (451 events, 446 errors, 5 standards, 3 people with both classes), as a caveat. Its scores are not published: with three people its bootstrap bounds can be one person’s value.

Orthosis 64-channel: the matched EEG-minus-confound mean is published without an interval (none was computed). Its range is the per-person extremes and is not published; how many of the 8 people had EEG above the confound follows from the audited all-positive flag.

Permutation and label-shuffle controls (Orthosis, BINGO, handwriting): the mean and the observed range (lowest and highest replicate mean) are published, labelled as ranges, not intervals. Individual replicates are not.

EEGPT: the aggregate comparison is published under the 2026-10-12 parent approval and the finalization that binds the approved export. Its code licence (Apache-2.0) covers the repository’s source code only; the checkpoint’s licence is unresolved and no original or converted weights are distributed. Core-matrix EEGPT outputs were not opened, and the core-matrix held cells are unchanged.

BINGO (owner decision 3, working default to be confirmed at preview): published with its rights as they stand — no licence stated by the source; consent from the project’s public deliverable D3.1 version 3.0, stated for its NATO-alphabet recordings in the same CERTH laboratory; no ethics-approval reference published. sources[bingo-cross-language].publication is the switch: status_only holds it without rework. The documented preprocessing (ASR, FORCe) is printed beside the result, attributed to D3.1 version 2.0, not re-verified against the file.

Handwriting (owner decision, 2026-10-12): the mask-aware analysis is published as aggregates with its rights gap stated. No ethics-approval or informed-consent statement was found: the dataset card declares CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and gated access and has none; a participating team’s challenge paper (arXiv:2608.03176v2), which identifies the competition as the ACM MM 2026 Multimodal Brain-Computer Interface Grand Challenge, has none and states no dataset licence; and the organisers’ paper it cites is listed there as forthcoming and was not found published (checked 2026-10-12). The gap is stated once in full in the page credits and on /data-use/, with a short pointer beside the result, and is to be rechecked when the organisers’ paper appears. Like BOAS (7 October) and BINGO (this review), it is an owner decision on stated gaps; BNCI2015-001’s hold of 2026-09-20 is unchanged, because its review turns on its CC BY-NC-ND catalogue licence as well. sources[handwriting-mask-aware].publication remains the switch: status_only holds it again without rework. The earlier analysis is context only and never a second cohort.

Handwriting, five people: the means, the descriptive person-bootstrap intervals of the relative-EEG, elapsed-time and mask-plus-time arms, the three paired contrasts, the label-shuffle means with observed ranges, the availability histogram over trials and the cohort counts are published. The mask-only control’s interval is not: at five people its bounds would show individual people’s scores. The training-majority control scores chance for every person by construction, as Orthosis’s prior does. No other bound is one person’s score: each is a percentile of resampled five-person means.

REFED: the export’s “pending parent handoff approval” status is resolved by the handoff check, which binds the same handoff, export and result-audit hashes. Only the primary equal-axis mean absolute error is published; per-axis errors and RMSE stay out.
BINGO: the project’s own subject-independent result on its NATO-alphabet dataset (D3.1 version 3.0) is published as the project’s result, labelled and kept apart from ours.

notPublished: Per-person, per-field, per-folder, per-clip and per-record values of any kind: the Orthosis matched EEG-minus-confound range, every per-person minimum and maximum, per-fold scores. How many people or fields did better is published where an audited flag implies it; which ones is not.
The Orthosis response-clean subset scores (only its counts are published), and every secondary paired difference.
The individual permutation and label-shuffle replicates: their mean and observed range are published.

BINGO mean confusion matrices and per-replicate shuffle intervals; handwriting pooled metrics, per-class recall and confusion matrices, and the mask-only control’s bootstrap interval, whose bounds would show individual people’s scores; REFED per-axis errors, RMSE and combined RMSE.

Participant, field, folder, session, clip, video, file and run identifiers, labels, targets, features, embeddings, predictions, fitted parameters and checkpoints, and every source file. EEGPT weights, original or converted, are not distributed.
Measured compute: wall times, memory and process counts from every handoff and audit.

The handoffs, approval and finalization records, QA records, release decisions and independent audits themselves: each is pinned by SHA-256 in this manifest and its verdict and binding are checked by the export. They carry private storage paths and are not copied. Candidate exports named *-candidate.json were not opened.
